'''Joshua Scott McRoberts''' (born February 28, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played eleven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). McRoberts, a {{convert|6|ft|10|in|adj=on}} [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 37th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
McRoberts attended [[Carmel High School (Carmel, Indiana)|Carmel High School]] in [[Carmel, Indiana]], and led the Greyhounds in both scoring and rebounding during his senior year.

He averaged 17.9 points to go along with 11.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 3.0 blocked shots per game and shot .593 (166-of-280) from the field while guiding the Greyhounds to a 21–4 record and a trip to the sectional championship game in 2005. McRoberts was considered the number-one power forward prospect out of high school, and was projected to be drafted in the [[2005 NBA draft]] had he declared.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/10/23/AR2005102301414.html | newspaper=The Washington Post | title=Duke Is the Team to Beat in NBA Draft-Depleted ACC | first=Eric | last=Prisbell | date=October 24, 2005 | access-date=May 7, 2010}}</ref>

As of 2021, 247sports.org rates McRoberts as the third-highest-rated recruit in the history of Duke basketball.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Sport/Basketball/AllTimeRecruits/|title = Duke All Time Basketball Recruits}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman season===
At [[Duke University]], McRoberts averaged 8.7 points and 1.3 blocked shots while leading the team in field goal percentage (60.5%).<ref name="godukeroster">{{cite web |title=Josh McRoberts |publisher=GoDuke.com |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=186182&Q_SEASON=2006 |access-date=March 14, 2007 |archive-date=July 9, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110709203203/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=186182&Q_SEASON=2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> McRoberts was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman team. He helped the [[Duke Blue Devils]] to a record of 32–4, the ACC regular season title, and the 2006 ACC tournament championship title by defeating [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]]. He was also named to the third team Freshman All-America by collegehoops.net.

McRoberts' late-season numbers improved as he recorded 10 of his 15 double-figure scoring games in his final 14 games, while averaging 10.4 points and 6.3 rebounds (with a 59.6 FG%).<ref name="goduke">{{cite web |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=271339 |title=McRoberts Announces Plan To Return For Sophomore Season |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=April 26, 2006 |access-date=January 29, 2007}}</ref>

Considered a potential [[NBA draft]] lottery pick, McRoberts instead stated he would not enter the draft, and would return to Duke for the 2006–07 season.<ref name="goduke"/>

McRoberts underwent a successful lumbar [[discectomy]] on August 3, 2006. He had been suffering from chronic back problems since high school and had the operation to alleviate the problem.

===Sophomore season===
On December 19, 2006, against [[Kent State University|Kent State]], McRoberts had a career-high 19 points, six blocks, six rebounds, four assists, and four steals making him the first Duke player to tally at least four in all five categories.<ref>{{cite news|title=Game Recaps |work=CNN |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/recaps/2006/12/19/40577_recap.html |access-date=December 19, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070103185245/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/recaps/2006/12/19/40577_recap.html |archive-date=January 3, 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2007–2008)===
On March 22, 2007, McRoberts declared himself eligible for the [[2007 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Duke sophomore McRoberts eligible for NBA draft |date=March 22, 2007 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2808295 |access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref> On June 28, 2007, he was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 37th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft|NBA draft]].

On January 9, 2008, McRoberts was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]], the Trail Blazers' [[D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Trail Blazers Assign Josh McRoberts To Idaho Stampede'' |work=nba.com |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/mcroberts_080109.html |access-date=February 4, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081208233006/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/mcroberts_080109.html |archive-date=December 8, 2008 }}</ref> After being with the Stampede for nearly a month, and getting an over 20-minute-per-game increase in playing time, McRoberts was called back up to the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Welcome back McBob |work=oregonlive.com |date=February 4, 2008 |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/blazers/2008/02/welome_back_mcbob.html |access-date=February 4, 2008}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2008–2011)===
[[File:Josh McRoberts Bulls vs Pacers December 2009.jpg|thumb|left|McRoberts in December 2009 as a member of the Pacers]]
On June 26, 2008, the night of the [[2008 NBA draft]], McRoberts was traded by the Trail Blazers to his hometown [[Indiana Pacers]] in a deal that sent him, along with [[Brandon Rush]] and [[Jarrett Jack]] in return, for 11th overall pick [[Jerryd Bayless]] and [[Ike Diogu]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers_trades_release_080709.html |title=Pacers announce two trades; acquire seven players |work=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2008|access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2011–2012)===
On December 14, 2011, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] signed McRoberts to a two-year deal worth about $6 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/111214_lakerssign_joshmcroberts.html |title=Lakers Sign Josh McRoberts |work=NBA.com |date=December 14, 2011|access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2012–2013)===
[[File:Josh McRoberts Washington at Orlando 067.jpg|thumb|McRoberts playing for the Magic in 2012]]
On August 10, 2012, McRoberts was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] as part of the blockbuster deal that sent All-Star center [[Dwight Howard]] to the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-six-players-five-draft-picks-howard-trade |title=Magic Acquire Six Players, Five Draft Picks in Howard Trade |last=Cohen |first=Josh |work=NBA.com |date=August 10, 2012 |access-date=April 15, 2023 }}</ref>

===Charlotte Bobcats (2013–2014)===
On February 21, 2013, McRoberts was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for [[Hakim Warrick]].<ref>{{cite web |access-date=February 22, 2013 |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/bobcats-acquire-josh-mcroberts-orlando |title=Bobcats Acquire Josh McRoberts from Orlando |work=NBA.com |date=February 23, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130225174244/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/bobcats-acquire-josh-mcroberts-orlando |archive-date=February 25, 2013 }}</ref>

On July 11, 2013, McRoberts re-signed with the Bobcats.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13728 |title=Charlotte Bobcats re-sign Josh McRoberts |access-date=July 12, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316003522/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13728 |archive-date=March 16, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 28, 2014, McRoberts scored a career-high 24 points in a loss to the [[Orlando Magic]]. He finished the season with career highs in games played and starts with 78 each. On April 30, 2014, McRoberts underwent successful surgery to remove bone spurs from his left big toe.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/mcroberts-has-successful-toe-surgery McRoberts Has Successful Toe Surgery] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502085603/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/mcroberts-has-successful-toe-surgery |date=May 2, 2014 }}</ref>

On June 18, 2014, McRoberts opted out of his 2014–15 contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11103610 Josh McRoberts opts out of contract]</ref>

===Miami Heat (2014–2017)===
On July 14, 2014, McRoberts signed with the [[Miami Heat]]<ref>[https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-josh-mcroberts HEAT Signs Josh McRoberts]</ref> to a reported four-year, $23 million contract.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234157/Josh-McRoberts-Verbally-Commits-To-Four-Year-$23M-Deal-With-Heat Josh McRoberts Verbally Commits To Four-Year, $23M Deal With Heat]</ref> After tearing his right meniscus on December 9, 2014, against the [[Phoenix Suns]], McRoberts underwent surgery to repair it on December 22 and was subsequently ruled out for the rest of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]]; he appeared in just 17 games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/josh-mcroberts-undergoes-successful-surgery |title=Josh McRoberts Undergoes Successful Surgery |last=Herrera|first=Irene|work=NBA.com |date=December 23, 2014 |access-date=April 15, 2023 }}</ref>

After having most of 2014–15 season wiped out by injuries, McRoberts lost his starting spot because of [[Hassan Whiteside]]'s emergence. He came into the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]] with a significant role off the bench, but that got away from him after missing nearly two months with a bruised knee.<ref>[https://heatzone.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2016/04/16/2016-nba-playoffs-qa-with-josh-mcroberts-on-falling-in-and-out-of-rotation 2016 NBA playoffs: Q&A with Josh McRoberts on rocky season]</ref>

On December 27, 2016, McRoberts was ruled out indefinitely with a stress fracture in his problematic left foot.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/news/josh-mcroberts-foot-out-indefinitely Heat's Josh McRoberts out indefinitely with foot injury]</ref>

On May 23, 2017, McRoberts opted into his final year of his contract worth just over $6 million.<ref>{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-josh-mcroberts-20170523-story.html|title=Josh McRoberts opts in, $6M salary now on Miami Heat 2017-18 salary cap|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=May 23, 2017|access-date=July 6, 2017}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2017–2018)===
On July 7, 2017, McRoberts was traded, along with a [[2023 NBA draft|2023 second-round draft]] pick and cash considerations, to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[A. J. Hammons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-trade-josh-mcroberts |title=HEAT Trade Josh McRoberts|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=April 16, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-trade-j-hammons-miami-josh-mcroberts/|title=Mavericks trade A.J. Hammons to Miami for Josh McRoberts|work=Mavs.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102012856/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-trade-j-hammons-miami-josh-mcroberts/|archive-date=January 2, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 10, 2018, he was waived by the Mavericks.<ref name=mavs-waive>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/dallas-mavericks-waive-josh-mcroberts |title=Dallas Mavericks waive Josh McRoberts|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2018|access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref> He saw action in two games for the Mavericks after spending the first 37 games of the season on the inactive list while rehabbing a left foot injury.<ref name="mavs-waive"/>

==Player profile==
McRoberts can play both [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]]. His scoring mostly comes off fast breaks, rebounds and hustle plays. He is a [[screen-setter]] with a decent [[jumper (basketball)|jumper]],<ref name=breshnahan_12142011>{{cite news|last=Bresnahan |first=Mike |title=Lakers upset with Chris Paul's trade to Clippers |date=December 14, 2011 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/la-sp-lakers-20111215,0,3146965.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111215182347/http://www.latimes.com/sports/basketball/nba/lakers/la-sp-lakers-20111215,0,3146965.story |archive-date=December 15, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and possesses excellent passing skills for a big man.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/story/_/id/11187465 |title=Josh McRoberts commits to Heat |last=Stein |first=Mark |date=July 8, 2014|access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref> He is considered an average defender. Former teammate [[Pau Gasol]] called McRoberts "scrappy and a hustler".<ref name=breshnahan_12142011/>

==Post-playing career==
According to the [https://carmelmonthlymagazine.com/josh-mcroberts-rejoins-the-chs-pack-as-an-assistant-coach ''Carmel Monthly''] magazine, McRoberts became an assistant coach for the Carmel High School's varsity basketball team during the 2020–21 season.
